instruction: Make the text layer smaller to decrease its footprint on the canvas.

metadata.explanation: Task requires scaling down the text layer to make it smaller. The evaluator finds the bounding box of the text (leftmost, rightmost, topmost, bottommost dark pixels) and calculates width and height ratios relative to the image dimensions. It checks if the text occupies less than 30% of image width and less than 15% of image height. This tests scaling/transform tools in GIMP.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checks if text layer has been scaled down to be smaller
Metric logic is sound: finds bounding box of text pixels and calculates width/height ratios relative to canvas size
Expected parameter handling is correct: directly accesses 'max_text_width_ratio' and 'max_text_height_ratio' from the rules dict (not 'expected.get(rules)')
Postconfig properly exports the modified image using GIMP hotkeys so the file can be retrieved and analyzed
Edge cases handled: returns 0.0 when src_path is None or when no text is found
Complete coverage: verifies the single requirement in the instruction
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor limitation: The evaluator uses absolute thresholds (30% width, 15% height) rather than comparing to original text size. This assumes original text is larger than these thresholds, which should be true for typical GIMP text layers but is not explicitly verified
Pixel threshold of 128 for dark pixels might miss very light colored or heavily anti-aliased text, though it should work for typical text on orange background

Using AND condition for both dimensions (width_ratio < 0.3 AND height_ratio < 0.15) means both must be satisfied. This is reasonable but slightly strict - scaling down only one dimension wouldn't pass
